title: Metal-Organic Cages (MOC) Synthesis Process
description: A comprehensive JSON schema representing the synthesis, characterization, and properties of Metal-Organic Cages (MOCs), including reactants, process parameters, characterization methods, host-guest behavior, recycling, and material properties. Designed for reproducibility, modularity, and alignment with chemical best practices. Incorporates insights from research literature and domain expert feedback to improve consistency, reduce redundancy, and enhance extensibility. This version integrates findings from recent research on chameleonic Fe(II) tetrahedral cages and pairwise linking of MOCs as supermolecular building blocks (SBBs) to form multivariate crystalline materials, emphasizing dynamic guest encapsulation, adaptive cavity environments via pendant P=O group orientation (endo/exo), structural flexibility in solution vs. solid state, and the rational design of multi-functional porous frameworks through stoichiometric control and preferential coordination. The schema has been refined per expert feedback to streamline characterization and host-guest sections, removing redundant fields and focusing on essential, standardized data.

moc_type.description: The chemical formula, designation, and structural composition of the Metal-Organic Cage (MOC), including metal ions, ligands, stoichiometry, counterions, symmetry, cavity volume, and stereochemical features. Unified representation of structural composition with standardized stoichiometric counts and net charge. Includes coordination modes, structural motifs, and structural evolution pathways. Incorporates insights on dynamic cavity adaptation, flexible ligand functionality, and the ability to serve as a supermolecular building block (SBB) in multivariate crystalline materials.

formula.description: The chemical formula of the MOC, e.g., [Fe4L4][BF4]8, including encapsulated guests and solvates (e.g., H2O@[Fe4L4][BF4]8). For multivariate materials formed by pairwise linking, includes the stoichiometric formula of the assembled framework (e.g., {[1-Cu]·[2-Rh]2}n).

designation.description: Common name or identifier used in literature (e.g., 'Fe4L4', 'Chameleonic Cage', '1-Cu', '2-Rh').

composition.description: Unified representation of the stoichiometric composition of the MOC, including metal and ligand counts, net charge, and metal-to-ligand ratio. Serves as a central reference for both structural and functional stoichiometry. For multivariate materials, this refers to the repeating unit of the framework.

metal.description: Total number of metal ions (M) in the cage unit.

ligand.description: Number of ligand molecules (L) in the cage unit.

charge.description: Net charge of the cage complex (e.g., +4, -2, +8).

metal_to_ligand_ratio.description: Stoichiometric ratio of metal to ligand in the cage, expressed as [metal_count, ligand_count]. The first element corresponds to the number of metal ions; the second to the number of ligand molecules.

counter_ion.description: Counterion used to balance the charge of the cage complex (e.g., Cl⁻, NO₃⁻, OTf⁻, NTf₂⁻, BF₄⁻). For multivariate materials, this may reflect the overall charge balance of the framework.

symmetry.description: Point group symmetry of the cage (e.g., Th, O, C2v, D3h, T, P21/c, P4̅n2, I23). Reflects stereochemical arrangement and structural regularity. For multivariate frameworks, includes the space group of the crystalline material.

cavity_volume.description: Volume of the internal cavity (in Å³), derived from crystallographic or computational data. For multivariate materials, this may refer to the cavity of the individual MOC building block.

structural_motif.description: The overall architectural motif of the cage, such as tetrahedral, cyclic, or quadruple-stranded, reflecting structural evolution during synthesis. For multivariate materials, includes the motif of the assembled framework (e.g., 2D (4,4)-net).

coordination_modes.description: List of distinct coordination modes adopted by the ligand in the cage, e.g., μ3-κ²O1:κO2:κN2:κO5, μ3-κO1:κO2:κO4:κN2:κO5. For multivariate materials, includes coordination modes at the interface between MOCs.

stereochemistry.description: Detailed description of the stereochemical configuration of the cage, including chirality, helical handedness, and enantiomeric excess (ee) if applicable. For multivariate materials, includes stereochemistry of the framework and relative orientation of MOCs.

chirality.description: Overall chirality of the cage (e.g., achiral, chiral, racemic, enantiopure).

helical_handedness.description: Helical handedness of the cage corners (e.g., P, M, P6-1, M6-1), particularly relevant for helicate-bridged cages.

enantiomeric_excess.description: Enantiomeric excess (ee) of the cage, measured by chiral NMR or CD spectroscopy (in %).

chiral_induction_method.description: Method used to induce stereocontrol during synthesis (e.g., addition of chiral additive like BINOL).

chiral_memory.description: Indicates whether the cage retains its stereochemical configuration after removal of chiral inducer (e.g., due to cooperative locking).

flexibility.description: Description of cage flexibility, including dynamic ligand behavior (e.g., 'flexible P=O groups capable of endo/exo switching', 'rigid framework'). For multivariate materials, includes flexibility of the interface between MOCs.
flexibility.example: Flexible P=O groups capable of endo/exo switching

supermolecular_building_block.description: Indicates whether the MOC is designed and used as a preformed supermolecular building block (SBB) for assembling higher-order crystalline materials.

multivariate_framework.description: Details about the multivariate crystalline framework formed by pairwise linking of MOCs. Includes stoichiometry, connectivity, and structural features of the assembled material.

linking_moc.description: Designation of the second MOC used in pairwise linking (e.g., '2-Rh' in {[1-Cu]·[2-Rh]2}n).

stoichiometry.description: Molar ratio of the two MOCs in the framework (e.g., 1:2, 1:1).

connectivity.description: Nature of the connectivity in the framework (e.g., 2D (4,4)-net, 1D coordination polymer).

coordination_interface.description: Description of the coordination interaction between MOCs (e.g., 'Rh-aniline coordination', 'hydrogen bonding with solvent').

framework_symmetry.description: Space group or symmetry of the multivariate framework (e.g., I4/m, P-1).

synthesis.description: Comprehensive description of the MOC synthesis process, including reactants, reaction protocol (with stages), and workup. All synthesis-related elements are grouped into a single, coherent unit for clarity and reproducibility. For multivariate materials, includes the stoichiometric control of MOCs in solution and crystallization conditions.

reactants.description: All reactants used in the synthesis, including metal sources, ligands, counterion sources, and chiral inducers, with standardized stoichiometric quantities. For multivariate materials, includes both MOC building blocks.

metal_source.description: The source compound of the metal ion used in the synthesis.

compound.description: Chemical name or formula of the metal salt (e.g., Fe(BF4)2·6H2O, ZnCl2).

purity.description: Purity of the metal salt (e.g., 98%, ACS grade, HPLC grade).

supplier.description: Supplier or manufacturer of the metal salt.

amount.description: Amount of metal source used in the synthesis (in moles or grams).

ligand.description: The organic ligand (L) used in the self-assembly process.

name.description: Common or IUPAC name of the ligand (e.g., tris(4-aminophenyl)phosphate, H5L).

purity.description: Purity of the ligand (e.g., 95%, HPLC grade).

supplier.description: Supplier or manufacturer of the ligand.

synthesis_required.description: Indicates whether the ligand must be pre-synthesized (true) or is commercially available (false).

amount.description: Amount of ligand used in the synthesis (in moles or grams).

counter_ion_source.description: List of compounds used to supply counterions (e.g., NaNO3, HNO3, NaClO4, TBAOTf, TBANTf2).

compound.description: Chemical name or formula of the counterion source.

amount.description: Amount of counterion source added (in moles or grams).

chiral_inducer.description: Chiral additive used to control stereochemistry during self-assembly (e.g., (R)-BINOL, (S)-BINOL).

compound.description: Name or formula of the chiral inducer (e.g., (R)-1,1′-bi-2-naphthol).

amount.description: Amount of chiral inducer added (in moles or grams).

equivalents.description: Number of equivalents relative to the metal source.

role.description: Role of the chiral inducer in the assembly process.

reaction_protocol.description: Integrated reaction protocol combining global conditions and stage-specific steps. Each stage can override global defaults. For multivariate materials, includes conditions for mixing MOCs and crystallization.

global_conditions.description: Default conditions applied to all stages unless overridden.

temperature.description: Default reaction temperature in degrees Celsius.

solvent.description: Default solvent used in the reaction.

atmosphere.description: Default atmosphere under which the reaction is performed.

concentration.description: Total concentration of reactants in the reaction mixture (in M or mg/mL).

stages.description: Sequential stages of the synthesis process. Each stage may override global conditions.

stage.description: Sequential stage number in the synthesis process.

description.description: Textual description of the stage (e.g., 'Mix Fe(BF4)2·6H2O and ligand in acetonitrile at room temperature').
description.example: Mix Fe(BF4)2·6H2O and ligand in acetonitrile at room temperature for 10 min

temperature.description: Temperature during this stage in degrees Celsius (overrides global if specified).

time.description: Duration of this stage in hours.

solvent.description: Solvent used in this stage (overrides global if specified).

pressure.description: Pressure during the stage (if applicable), in Pascals (Pa).

atmosphere.description: Atmosphere under which the stage was performed (overrides global if specified).

additional_notes.description: Any additional details about the stage (e.g., 'stirred magnetically', 'filtered through syringe filter').

workup.description: Post-reaction procedures used to isolate and purify the MOC, including solvent removal, purification, yield, concentration, and storage. For multivariate materials, includes activation and recrystallization steps.

solvent_removal.description: Method used to remove solvent (e.g., rotary evaporation, vacuum drying, dialysis).

purification_method.description: Method used to purify the final product (e.g., column chromatography, recrystallization, dialysis, size exclusion).

yield.description: Yield of the MOC synthesis in percentage.

concentration.description: Concentration of the MOC in the final solution (in mg/mL or M).

final_solvent.description: Solvent in which the purified MOC is stored or used for further experiments.

chiral_inducer_removal.description: Method used to remove the chiral inducer (e.g., washing with ethyl acetate, diethyl ether).
chiral_inducer_removal.example: Washed with ethyl acetate and diethyl ether

activation.description: Method used to activate the material (e.g., supercritical CO2 exchange, thermal treatment).
activation.example: Supercritical CO2 exchange of acetone-solvated sample

recrystallization.description: Method used to recrystallize the material (e.g., slow-vapor diffusion, cooling).
recrystallization.example: Slow-vapor diffusion of ethyl acetate into DMA solution

characterisation.description: Methods used to confirm the identity, structure, and purity of the synthesized MOC. Each entry follows a modular structure: technique → parameters → interpretation. Generalized to avoid data-specific entries. Only essential parameters are included per expert feedback. For multivariate materials, includes PXRD, TEM, and FFT analysis.

instrument.description: Name or model of the instrument used.

parameters.description: Specific conditions under which the measurement was performed.

concentration.description: Concentration of the sample (in mg/mL or M).

resolution.description: Resolution or quality of the data (e.g., 'high resolution', 'low resolution').

interpretation.description: Interpretation of the result in the context of MOC identity or structure.
interpretation.example: Confirmed the formation of the [Fe4L4]8+ cage via molecular ion peak

host_guest_properties.description: Properties related to the ability of the MOC to bind small molecules (guests), including binding conditions, stoichiometry, affinity, selectivity, and structural adaptation. Focuses on reaction conditions and selectivity. Incorporates dynamic guest encapsulation (anionic, neutral, cationic) and adaptive cavity behavior via flexible ligand groups. For multivariate materials, includes guest binding in the framework pores.

guests_bound.description: List of guest molecules that the MOC can encapsulate, including binding mode, stoichiometry, method, solvent, temperature, and structural adaptation.

molecule.description: Name or formula of the guest molecule (e.g., H2O, [BF4]-, [Cu]+, [Zn]2+).

binding_mode.description: How the guest binds (e.g., 'encapsulated in cavity', 'coordinated to metal site', 'ion exchange').
binding_mode.example: encapsulated in cavity via ion exchange

stoichiometry.description: Molar ratio of guest to cage (e.g., 1:1, 2:1, 4:1).

method.description: Method used to determine guest binding (e.g., NMR titration, ITC, DOSY, UV-Vis, SCXRD, HR-MS).

solvent.description: Solvent in which the binding interaction was observed (e.g., methanol, acetonitrile).

temperature.description: Temperature at which binding was studied (°C).

structural_adaptation.description: Details about structural changes in the cage in response to guest size/shape, including isomerism and interconversion dynamics.

isomers_present.description: List of cage isomers observed (e.g., T-1, C3-1).

interconversion_rate.description: Kinetic description of isomer interconversion (e.g., 'slow exchange on NMR time scale', 'equilibrium reached after 2 weeks').
interconversion_rate.example: slow exchange on NMR time scale

shape_memory.description: Indicates whether a shape memory effect was observed during guest displacement (i.e., rapid guest exchange with slow structural rearrangement).

cavity_adaptation.description: Description of how the cavity adapts to guest (e.g., 'P=O groups switch from endo to exo configuration', 'cavity expands to accommodate larger guest').
cavity_adaptation.example: P=O groups switch from endo to exo configuration

anion_selectivity.description: Information on anion selectivity and binding hierarchy, particularly relevant for cages with exposed metal sites.

binding_hierarchy.description: List of anions ranked by binding affinity (e.g., NTf2- > OTf- > BF4-).

anion_displacement.description: Summary of displacement experiments showing which anions can be displaced by others.

displaced_by.description: List of anions that can displace the bound anion.

not_displaced_by.description: List of anions that fail to displace the bound anion.

catalytic_performance.description: Performance metrics for catalytic applications, such as conversion yield, selectivity, TON, and reaction conditions.

substrate.description: Substrate used in catalytic reaction (e.g., formaldehyde, aniline, ethyl diazoacetate).

reaction_conditions.description: Conditions under which catalytic performance was measured.

applications.description: Potential applications of the MOC based on host-guest behavior.

recycling.description: Details about the recovery and reuse of the MOC after guest binding.

procedure.description: Description of the recycling process (e.g., dissolution in CH3CN, addition of tetrabutylammonium nitrate).
procedure.example: Dissolve the precipitate in CH3CN, add tetrabutylammonium nitrate to recover the MOC

cycles.description: Number of successful recycling cycles demonstrated.

recovery_yield.description: Percentage of MOC recovered after recycling cycles.

purity_check.description: Method used to confirm the purity of the recovered MOC (e.g., 1H NMR, 19F NMR, ESI-MS).
purity_check.example: 1H NMR in D2O matched authentic sample; PXRD pattern identical

material_properties.description: Other measurable physical and chemical properties of the MOC, including stability, porosity, electronic behavior, stereochemistry, and structural dynamics. Incorporates insights on dynamic cavity adaptation and solution vs. solid-state behavior. For multivariate materials, includes porosity, BET surface area, and pore size distribution.

stability.description: Stability of the MOC under various conditions.

thermal_stability.description: Temperature at which the MOC begins to decompose (°C).

chemical_stability.description: Stability in different solvents or pH conditions (e.g., 'stable in methanol, decomposes in water').
chemical_stability.example: Stable in methanol and chloroform; decomposes in water

long_term_stability.description: Stability over time (e.g., 'stable for >6 months at room temperature').

solution_stability.description: Stability of the cage in solution (e.g., 'cubic symmetry lost in solution', 'stable for 24 h').
solution_stability.example: Cubic symmetry lost in solution; cage remains intact as confirmed by HR-MS

physical_properties.description: Other measurable physical properties of the MOC.

conductivity.description: Electrical conductivity of the MOC (in S/cm).

cavity_volume.description: Volume of the internal cavity (in Å³).

pore_size_distribution.description: Distribution of pore sizes derived from adsorption isotherms.

method.description: Method used to derive pore size distribution (e.g., BJH, DFT).

stereochemistry.description: Description of the stereochemistry of the cage (e.g., 'achiral, symmetric', 'P-helical').

structural_dynamics.description: Information about dynamic behavior of the cage framework, including isomer interconversion and flexibility.

flexibility.description: Description of cage flexibility (e.g., 'highly flexible due to methylene linkers', 'rigid framework').
flexibility.example: Highly flexible due to methylene groups between phenyl rings and azaphosphatrane nitrogen atoms

isomer_interconversion.description: Kinetic and thermodynamic details of cage isomer interconversion.

mechanism.description: Proposed mechanism of isomer interconversion (e.g., 'face inversion via Fe–N bond disruption').
mechanism.example: Face inversion via disruption of Er–N linkages

activation_energy.description: Free energy of activation (ΔG‡) for isomer interconversion (in kJ/mol).

cavity_adaptation.description: Details on how the cavity adapts to different guests via ligand group orientation (e.g., endo/exo switching).

endo_exo_switching.description: Indicates whether the cage can dynamically switch between endo and exo configurations of pendant groups.

guest_dependent_configuration.description: Description of how guest type influences configuration (e.g., 'anionic guests favor exo, cationic favor endo').
guest_dependent_configuration.example: Anionic guests favor exo configuration; cationic guests favor endo configuration

optical_properties.description: Chiroptical and photophysical properties of the MOC, including circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

circular_dichroism.description: CD spectrum characteristics, including Cotton effect and spectral range.

cotton_effect.description: Description of the CD Cotton effect (e.g., 'negative Cotton effect at 400 nm').

spectral_range.description: Wavelength range of CD measurement (e.g., 350–450 nm).

circularly_polarized_luminescence.description: CPL properties, including dissymmetry factor and emission characteristics.

dissymmetry_factor.description: Dissymmetry factor (|g_lum|) of the CPL emission.

quantum_yield.description: Absolute quantum yield (QY) of the emission.

additional_notes.description: Any other relevant information not covered in other sections, including limitations, future work, experimental nuances, solvent-dependent behavior, structural adaptation phenomena, chiral memory effects, and catalytic mechanisms. Emphasizes structural evolution, coordination mode diversity, and catalytic efficiency. Incorporates findings on bimetallic active sites, catalytic nanoreactor function, substrate selectivity in multicomponent reactions, and dynamic guest encapsulation via flexible ligand groups. Highlights the chameleonic nature of the cage, capable of adapting to anionic, neutral, and cationic guests through endo/exo switching of P=O groups. For multivariate materials, emphasizes the rational design of multi-functional frameworks through stoichiometric control and preferential coordination (e.g., Rh-aniline coordination).
additional_notes.example: The Fe4L4 cage exhibits chameleonic behavior, dynamically adapting its cavity via endo/exo switching of pendant P=O groups to encapsulate anionic ([BF4]-), neutral (H2O), and cationic ([Cu]+, [Zn]2+) guests. The solid-state structure reveals a non-centrosymmetric I23 space group, with homochiral ΛΛΛΛ diastereoisomer observed. In solution, the cubic symmetry is lost, but HR-MS confirms cage integrity. The flexible ligand enables adaptive guest binding, with guest type dictating the preferred configuration. The cage functions as a catalytic nanoreactor, with Lewis acidic Fe(II) centers facilitating multicomponent reactions. Stability is confirmed by thermal and solution studies, though guest exchange dynamics suggest fluxional behavior. In multivariate materials, pairwise linking of MOCs via preferential Rh-aniline coordination enables the rational design of crystalline frameworks with defined chemical complexity, such as {[1-Cu]·[2-Rh]2}n, where stoichiometric control dictates the network structure (2D (4,4)-net vs. 1D polymer). The framework exhibits improved porosity compared to discrete MOCs, with a BET surface area of 422 m²/g.
